display_name: The First Schedule and the Second Schedule of the Criminal Procedure Code 2010: the Penal Code offences' procedural treatment (arrestable, warrant or summons, bailable, trial court; ss 2(1), 7 to 9) and the laws to which criminal case disclosure procedures apply (ss 159, 211A)
scope: The First Schedule as printed in SSO's PDF, current version as at 01 Oct 2026: all 478 printed rows (chapters 3 to 23) and the four rows printed under 'Offences against laws other than the Penal Code 1871', each with its seven columns; and the provisions that read it: s 2(1) 'arrestable offence', 'non-arrestable offence', 'bailable offence' and 'fine-only offence', and ss 7 to 9 (trial courts). And the Second Schedule as printed (32 items, the laws to which criminal case disclosure procedures apply) with ss 159 and 211A that read it. NOT encoded: every other section of the Code (Parts 1 to 22) and the Third, Fourth, Fifth, Sixth and Seventh Schedules, by the requester's instructions of 2026-10-01; the elements of the offences (Penal Code, sg/penal-code-1871); any other written law; the Criminal Procedure Rules.

not_reviewed.note: No domain expert has read this against the statute, and no independent test pass has been run. The First Schedule extraction was checked against a second extraction method (460 of 464 rows agree; the 4 differences are the second method merging adjacent rows) and against the section numbers of the layout text, not against a human reading of the printed table. The source is SSO's unofficial consolidation. NOTES.md section 6.

forks.F1: ss 7(1)(a), 8(1): an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life has no maximum 'term' of 5 or 10 years and is read as outside those paragraphs.
forks.F2: First Schedule derived rows: a cell that says 'according as to whether ... for the offence abetted/attempted/...' is encoded as 'As for the underlying offence' and answers only when the underlying offence's treatment is supplied; the printed words are kept in the row.
forks.F3: First Schedule column 7: a blank cell is read as 'no court besides the General Division of the High Court' (the column is headed 'besides the General Division of High Court').
forks.F4: The four rows under 'Offences against laws other than the Penal Code 1871' are printed after s 512(2) and are encoded as their own rows with the section 'Other written law', not as part of s 512(2).
forks.F5: 'May not arrest without warrant unless specifically empowered ... by the law offended against' is read as 'the police may not ordinarily arrest without warrant' (s 2(1) says 'ordinarily').
forks.F7: s 159(1)(b): 'to be tried in a District Court' is a fact about the forum; a case to be tried in a Magistrate's Court is outside s 159(1) and the procedures then apply only by consent (s 159(3)).
forks.F8: Second Schedule item 9 excludes 'sections 6 and 15' of the Immigration Act 1959; the section is tested without its subsections, so every subsection of ss 6 and 15 is excluded.
forks.F9: s 211A(2): 'any offence that is to be tried in the General Division of the High Court, but is not mentioned in subsection (1)'; (1)(a) already covers every offence that must be tried there, so (2) is read as adding consent for an offence designated for the High Court under a law the Second Schedule does not list.
